title: Human–Wildlife Conflict Is Not a Myth
content:
ABSTRACT

Despite well-established critiques of the term, human–wildlife conflict remains a valid way to refer to certain types of harmful interactions between people and wild animals. Efforts to diversify human–wildlife interaction terminology beyond the conflict paradigm were partly catalyzed by an influential article in Conservation Letters titled “Rearticulating the Myth of Human-Wildlife Conflict,” which argued that the term conflict should be reserved for disagreements between people (i.e., human–human conflicts). Revisiting that discursive intervention, I examine here multiple interpretations of conflict and highlight its existence in nonhuman species. Conflicts take diverse forms, occur across different scales, and therefore carry varied meanings depending on context. They can also result in substantial harm, underscoring the need for empathy toward affected people and wildlife. Human–wildlife conflict is therefore not a “myth” but a real phenomenon with significant consequences for people and wildlife around the world. Rather than abandoning the term, future scholarship should continue to refine situated understandings of conflict within human–wildlife interaction research to help identify actionable pathways toward coexistence.

摘要

‘人类与野生动物冲突’一词虽屡遭学界批评, 但其仍适用于指代人与野生动物之间某些类型的伤害性互动。关于人与野生动物互动术语的多元化发展, 部分源于Peterson等人 (2010) 具有重要影响力的一篇文章, 该文主张“冲突”一词应仅限于指代人与人之间的分歧 (即人际冲突) 。本文重新审视了 Peterson 等人 (2010) 的话语干预, 探讨了冲突的多种内涵, 并指出冲突同样存在于非人类物种之中。冲突形式多样, 发生于不同尺度, 因而因具体情境而异, 承载着多重意涵。冲突亦可能导致实质性伤害, 这凸显了对受影响人群和野生动物抱有同理心之必要。因此, 人类与野生动物冲突并非虚论, 而是一个对全球人类与野生动物均产生重大影响的真实现象。未来研究应继续在人与野生动物互动研究中深化对冲突的情境化理解, 以助于识别通向共存的可行路径。
